why: What WHOIS has actually said about the addresses Weles routes through. `classify.ts` decides whether an exit looks like a datacenter or like somebody's home line, and the only evidence it has is the organisation string a registry hands back. These are observed substrings, not a taxonomy of the internet: every entry was seen on a real lookup. Keeping them as a record means a new hosting company is a line added to data, and it ends the shape this file was in before — thirteen four-element arrays spread back together, split that way only to stay under an inline-array-size hook, which is gaming a guard rather than answering it.
whois_fields_why: The field names the registries answer with. ARIN says OrgName, RIPE says descr or netname, and a lookup that reads only one of them learns nothing about half the internet.
